native_findings: Original public calls accepted or relabelled unverified token responses; included-pool identity and base/quote orientation were not checked.
The token-detail route did not request its linked top_pools; aggregated token reserve could be mistaken for a selected pool reserve.
Original cap/FDV and primary/base-token price fallbacks could change field meaning; zero and unknown require separate treatment.
Original sync/async throttle paths mixed epoch and monotonic clocks. Controlled native sequence reproduced an excessive wait, not a measured missed-trade or real-profit loss.
Original shared-window waiters could both consume a single renewed permission. Local configuration was not a public entitlement to30 calls/minute.
These are software defects demonstrated by isolated native tests, not a causal attribution for every historical non-buy.

implementation.resource: HTTP200 only; exact token id/type/attributes.address and canonical network/mint; no redirects or silently substituted paid/nonpublic gateway. Malformed resources and invalid contexts return unknown.
implementation.pool: include=top_pools; only the first linked pool may contribute when uniquely included and exact typed base/quote relationships include the requested token. Invalid optional pool data do not fabricate or invalidate otherwise valid token price.
implementation.fields: Primary token price only; nullable cap separate from FDV; zero preserved; selected pool reserve distinct from aggregated token reserve proxy. Invalid selected-pool reserve remains unknown, never filled from token aggregate. Base directional activity/change are not attributed to quote token. Pool event remains venue metadata, never mint birth.
implementation.receipt: Original successful JSON receipt is retained through owned close and cache; upstream market-asof is not invented. +25000% synthetic change reaches native common price-service fallback unchanged.
implementation.rate: Public Accept20230203, local max10/minute with shared monotonic spacing and fixed-window permission retried after each wakeup; numerical429 Retry-After is bounded and cooldown is rechecked. Cached reads do not consume new permission.
implementation.ownership: Compatible normal async callers share same-loop work for the same injected session/timeout; force owns a fresh generation. Atomic latest-admitted generation controls cache/backoff. Shared sync+async gate max16; existing owned-request limits bound async owners/joiners across loops. No autonomous loop or operational service is added.
implementation.cleanup: Owned sync responses/sessions and async sessions close before returning their admission. Repeated cancellation drains acknowledgement. Cleanup failure yields unknown rather than uncaught success. Synthetic closure does not prove actual socket closure or cleanup SLA.
implementation.visibility: Native runtime snapshot adds aggregate Gecko admission, ownership, recent failure-key pressure and fixed-category outcome events; no mint IDs or credentials. Categories are not unique wire calls or costs and may overlap.
implementation.preservation: Personal .env, data, logs and models are not synchronized or rewritten; only .env.example changes the public rate example from15 to10. Predictor schema, pipeline13, policies, exact0.1 SOL PAPER and risk/route/cash guards stay unchanged.
implementation.legacy_numeric_compatibility: Token-total-reserve and volume_usd_24h aliases remain numeric and retain their own grain; aggregate token reserve is not selected-pool liquidity. Two legacy fixtures now use a typed valid Solana mint, an owned fake Session/Response and a local monotonic clock. Numerical values, complete-interval assertions and cached receipt identity remain enforced.

remaining_limits: Actual public provider access, fluctuating quotas, production latency and coverage are untested. Upstream1-minute cache is not instant market-asof.

First-linked verified pool is not a certified best executable route; liquidity, supply/valuation, token orientation and numerical receipts remain provider-reported rather than independently checked on chain.

Other provider/common projections are not corrected by this Gecko scope: static review still finds FDV-to-cap fallbacks in fetcher/birdeye.py and utils/price_service.py. Their native contract repair and operational impact remain separate work.
Async compatible same-loop work coalesces; Gecko sync HTTP, Dex HTTP and all other project caches/registries are not certified by this stage.
Cancellation ownership can outlast a timeout. Real cleanup latency/socket closure and production throughput require separate acceptance.
No new first-launch installation or authenticated operational/provider/wallet run is performed; software regression is not a guarantee of zero future errors.

Uncapped synthetic tails do not establish earlier discovery, cost-executable capture, rare-event learning generalization, exhaustive opportunity coverage or prospective net profitability. Global goal remains incomplete.
